name: Hot compress on the abdomen after birth
what_people_do: After delivery a mother presses hot cloths or hot water bottles to the lower abdomen, often daily for weeks.
why_they_say_it_works: To help the womb drain (lochia) and shrink back, and to keep the body "warm" after birth.

documented_by.source: Okeke T et al 2013, Ann Med Health Sci Res, PMID 23634329
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Enugu, 420 mothers: 80.2% applied hot compresses to the lower abdomen to aid lochia drainage and uterine involution.

documented_by.source: Udigwe GO, Emelumadu OF, Udigwe IB 2013, West Afr J Med, PMID 24488282
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Nnewi, 330 Igbo mothers: 63.6% used hot compresses on the abdomen.

evidence.tested: Warm compress on the perineum in the second stage of labour (a different practice)
evidence.finding: Fewer third- or fourth-degree tears (RR 0.46) in the warm-compress group; applies to the perineum during pushing, not to the abdomen after birth.

source.name: Perineal techniques during the second stage of labour, Cochrane 2017, PMID 28608597

evidence.tested: Hot compress on the abdomen after birth for lochia or involution
evidence.finding: My search found no trial of it.

source.name: agent4-traditional-practices.md, 12 Nov 2026 (research file in this project)

harm_note: Burn risk on a numb, tired post-delivery body is plausible but I found no source quantifying it. The Nnewi authors call some postpartum practices "out rightly dangerous" without naming which in the abstract.
gaps: Do not read the perineal warm compress Cochrane result as support for this practice.
Burn injuries from hot compresses not found.
